yngre.explanation: "Yngre" means younger and never changes its ending. It is the comparing form of "ung" (young): "Hun er yngre end mig" means "She is younger than me". The next step up is "yngst" (youngest). The opposite is "ældre".

sentence.en: My sister is younger than me.

yngst.explanation: "Yngst" means youngest. After "er" it stays "yngst" ("Hun er yngst"), and before a word it adds an "e": "den yngste". It is the top step after "ung" and "yngre". The opposite is "ældst".

yoghurt.explanation: "Yoghurt" is yogurt, an en-word, so "the yogurt" is "yoghurten". It is often eaten for breakfast with müsli or fruit. You can also write it "yogurt", but "yoghurt" is the more usual Danish spelling. It is also an easy word to use in a shop: "en yoghurt" is one pot.
